title: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper
note: Thirteen preferred images forwarded from a 2024-07-23 post; no verified exam date. Contains physiology 1-22, anatomy 1-11, histology 1-5 and embryology 1-2 (40 items). Actual anatomy numbering is 5-8 on source image 9 and 1-4 on image 10, contrary to the archive filenames; the printed numbers are preserved. Highlights are unofficial. Persian numerals/option letters are normalized.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is correct about "Transpulmonary Pressure"?
options: At the beginning of the inspiration is equal to +7.5 cm of water
The minimum value of this pressure is at the beginning of the inspiration
At the beginning of exhalation is equal to +0 cm of water
It is difference between the pleural pressure and the atmospheric pressure
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: In quiet breathing, TPP is least at end expiration/start inspiration and increases as the lungs inflate. It is alveolar minus pleural pressure.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 1; source page 1.

questions.prompt: Which of the following relationship is correct between lung volumes and capacities?
options: Vital capacity (VC) is equal to inspiratory capacity (IC) + expiratory reserve volume (ERV)
Functional residual capacity (FRC) equals inspiratory reserve volume (IRV) + expiratory reserve volume + residual volume (RV)
Total lung capacity (TLC) equals functional residual capacity + inspiratory reserve volume
Total lung capacity equals vital capacity + functional residual capacity
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: VC = IRV + TV + ERV = IC + ERV. FRC = ERV + RV; TLC = VC + RV.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 2; source page 1.

questions.prompt: What is the consequence of reducing alveolar oxygen pressure to less than 73 mmHg?
options: Potassium channel opens in the smooth muscle cell membrane of the pulmonary arteries
Calcium entry is inhibited into the smooth muscle cells of the pulmonary arteries
Release of the vasodilators (such as; nitric oxide) decreases
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: D is consistent with the textbook account of hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction; low oxygen inhibits relevant K+ channels and promotes Ca2+ entry. The numerical threshold and mediator model are simplified.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 3; source page 1.

questions.prompt: Which one the following type of blood flow is there at the "middle of the lung" in a healthy standing person?
options: The blood flow is zone-1 type
There is blood flow only during systole
There is continuous blood flow during systole and diastole
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The source highlights C, but middle does not specify vascular pressures or position relative to the heart. The zone-2/zone-3 boundary varies; B and D also describe the same intermittent pattern. Insufficiently localized for a unique key.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 4; source page 2.

questions.prompt: If during exercise, 500 ml of O2 is exchanged per minute for a pressure difference of 10 mmHg between two sides of the respiratory membrane, what will be the diffusing capacity of this gas?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Diffusing capacity = transfer rate / pressure gradient = 500/10 = 50 mL/min/mmHg. Persian numerals were visually verified and normalized.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 5; source page 2.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is correct about the diffusion of a gas from the respiratory membrane?
options: The diffusion coefficient of each gas is inversely related to the molecular weight of that gas.
The oxygen diffusion coefficient is lower than that of carbon monoxide
Increasing the thickness of the respiratory membrane increases gas diffusion
The diffusion coefficient of carbon dioxide is about 20 times more than oxygen.
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: CO2 has approximately 20 times the diffusion coefficient of oxygen. Molecular-weight dependence uses its square root, and thickness reduces diffusion.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 6; source page 3.

questions.prompt: According to Haldane effect, which of the following does increase?
options: Hemoglobin affinity for CO2 in pulmonary capillaries
Release of O2 in the blood of tissue capillaries
Displace of CO2 from the blood of the pulmonary capillaries
Hemoglobin affinity for O2 in pulmonary capillary blood
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Oxygenation of hemoglobin promotes CO2 release in pulmonary capillaries. Source A incorrectly states increased CO2 affinity.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 7; source page 4.

questions.prompt: What is the effect of reducing the activity of the penotaxic center in breathing?
options: Activation of inspiratory neurons in VRG
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Reduced pontine inspiratory switch-off prolongs inspiration and tends to lower respiratory rate in the teaching model.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 8; source page 4.

questions.prompt: During normal breathing, for how long (sec) the ramp signal is suppressed by the inhibitory signals from the pneumotaxic center?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The traditional illustrative cycle has about 2 seconds of inspiratory ramp and 3 seconds of suppression/expiration. This is a teaching timing example, not a fixed physiological constant.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 9; source page 4.

questions.prompt: How many milliliters (ml) of CO2 are there in each deciliter (dl) of venous blood?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The conventional rounded reference is about 52 mL CO2/dL in mixed venous blood, compared with about 48 in arterial blood.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 10; source page 4.

questions.prompt: Which of the following does cause bronchoconstriction?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Cold air can provoke bronchoconstriction; parasympathetic inhibition and sympathoadrenal stimulation generally promote dilation.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 11; source page 5.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is correct about respiratory work?
options: The tissue resistance work is more than the airway resistance work.
The least amount of respiratory work is related to the airway resistance work.
The airway resistance work is more than the elastic work.
In asthmatic patients, airway resistance work increases.
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Asthma narrows airways and increases the work required to overcome airway resistance.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 12; source page 5.

questions.prompt: In response to a decrease in arterial O2 pressure less than 60 mmHg, which neurotransmitter is released by "Glomus cells" in the carotid bodies?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The source selects acetylcholine, and hypoxia-induced release has been measured in human carotid bodies. However, noradrenergic and histaminergic glomus-cell signaling is also supported in primary carotid-body research; the species-unspecified wording does not establish one uniquely released transmitter among these choices.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 13; source page 5.

questions.prompt: If in a normal-sized alveolus, the reduction of surfactant causes the surface tension increases to triple, what does the collapse pressure change?
options: It doesn't change because the alveolar size remains constant.
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: At fixed radius, Laplace pressure P = 2T/r triples when surface tension triples.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 14; source page 6.

questions.prompt: What is the initial difference in CO2 pressure between the beginning of the pulmonary capillary and the alveoli?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The usual incoming venous-to-alveolar PCO2 gradient is about 5-6 mmHg; 5 is the closest supplied reference value.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 15; source page 6.

questions.prompt: Which of the following lung volume or capacity is less than the others?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: In standard reference volumes, FRC (about 2300 mL) is less than IRV, IC and VC. Individual values depend on body size and conditions.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 16; source page 6.

questions.prompt: Which of the following change is caused by the removal of elastin and collagen from the lung parenchyma?
options: Decreased ratio of ventilation to blood flow (V/Q)
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Loss of supporting elastic tissue reduces recoil and increases compliance, as in emphysema.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 17; source page 7.

questions.prompt: Which factor does reduce intracellular oxygen consumption?
options: An increase in intracellular ADP concentration.
A decrease in intracellular ATP concentration
An increase in tissue blood flow
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The entire question is crossed out and annotated حذف (deleted) in the source. None of the choices is a reliable direct cause of reduced oxygen consumption; increased ADP/metabolic demand usually increases it. Retained as a documented defective item, not scored.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 18; source page 7.

questions.prompt: Which of the ions are exchanged between two sides of red blood cells in venous blood?
options: HCO3- goes out and H+ goes in
H+ moves out and Cl- moves in
HCO3- goes in and Cl- goes out
HCO3- moves out and Cl- moves in
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: At systemic tissues, bicarbonate exits RBCs as chloride enters.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 19; source page 7.

questions.prompt: Which of the following gas has more "diffusing capacity" than others in resting?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: CO2's much greater solubility gives a higher reference diffusing capacity even at rest than the listed oxygen/CO exercise values. The stem's resting phrase conflicts with some distractors but does not change this comparison.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 20; source page 8.

questions.prompt: What is the Minute Respiratory Volume (L/min) in a subject with 15 respiration/min, 600 ml tidal volume and 200 ml anatomic dead space?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Minute ventilation = respiratory rate x tidal volume = 15 x 600 = 9000 mL/min = 9 L/min. Dead space would be subtracted for alveolar ventilation, not minute ventilation.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 21; source page 8.

questions.prompt: Which effect of exercise on the respiratory system is correct?
options: It changes blood flow type from zone-1 to zone-2
It multiplies the hydrostatic pressure in the pulmonary artery
It reduces the affinity of hemoglobin to oxygen in the blood of muscle's capillaries
It inhibits the ventral respiratory center (VRG) in the medulla
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Exercise-generated heat, CO2 and H+ shift the curve right and promote oxygen unloading. Normal apical recruitment is chiefly zone 2 toward zone 3.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 22; source page 8.

questions.prompt: All the following elements are attached to the thyroid cartilage except...?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The source's transverse pyramidal muscle denotes transverse arytenoid in this context; it connects the arytenoids rather than thyroid. The unusual source wording is preserved.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 5; source page 9.

questions.prompt: All the following vessels are involved in the blood supply of the nasal cavity except...?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The named nasal arterial supply comes from external/internal carotid branches, not a direct subclavian branch.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 6; source page 9.

questions.prompt: The apex of the lung posteriorly is adjacent to which of the following?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The neck of the first rib is a posterior relation of the lung apex; subclavian vessels cross anterior aspects of the cupola.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 7; source page 9.

questions.prompt: Which of the following items is involved in the formation of the lower side of the posterior nasal cavity fromen (choana)?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The horizontal plate of palatine forms the inferior choanal boundary.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 8; source page 9.

questions.prompt: All the following option can be seen in the lateral wall of the nasal cavity except...
options: Prependicular plate of the ethmoid bone
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The ethmoid perpendicular plate belongs to the septum/medial wall; the other structures contribute to the lateral wall.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 1; source page 10.

questions.prompt: The nasopalatine nerve is a branch of which of the following nerves?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Nasopalatine carries maxillary-division (V2) sensory fibers via the pterygopalatine ganglion.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 2; source page 10.

questions.prompt: Which of the following cartilages articulates with the thyroid cartilage?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The thyroid inferior horns form synovial cricothyroid joints with cricoid.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 3; source page 10.

questions.prompt: Which of the following options is correct about the larynx?
options: The vestibule is located below the false vocal folds
The position of the true vocal folds is higher than the false one
The opening of the saccule opens to the ventricle
thyroid cartilage is formed the inlet of larynx.
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The saccule is an upward extension opening into the laryngeal ventricle; the vestibule is above the false folds and true folds are inferior.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 4; source page 10.

questions.prompt: How many sections does the pharynx have?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: The pharynx has nasal, oral and laryngeal regions. Persian numerals normalized.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 9; source page 11.

questions.prompt: All the following structures are adjacent to the medial surface of the left lung except?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: Inferior vena cava is a right-sided relation; the left lung relates to aortic arch, descending aorta and esophagus.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 10; source page 11.

questions.prompt: What is the correct path air takes when it enters the trachea on its way to the lungs?
questions.subject: anatomy
questions.note: A has the intended airway sequence, but every option says air proceeds into pulmonary capillaries. Air stops in alveoli; individual gases diffuse across the barrier. The literal question has no fully correct option.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 11; source page 11.

questions.prompt: In which of the following is observed the Vocal Cord?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Vocal cords are laryngeal structures.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 1; source page 12.

questions.prompt: Which part of the lung tissue has a simple squamous cells?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Alveolar ducts are bounded by alveoli whose type I cells are squamous; the other listed conducting airways have taller lining cells.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 2; source page 12.

questions.prompt: What is the name Macrophage Alveolar Of Lunge?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: The source selects Pneumocyte III. The review uses alveolar macrophage/dust cell and distinguishes it from epithelial pneumocytes; no standard correct label is offered.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 3; source page 12.

questions.prompt: Where is Hyaline Cartilge In Around of Burnouse?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Burnouse appears to mean bronchus. Bronchial hyaline plates form a cartilage layer external to smooth muscle, while adventitia is the outer connective tissue. The question omits the cartilage layer and does not define its layer convention; source A is retained but not certified.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 4; source page 12.

questions.prompt: In which of the following is observed the Unicell Gland Or Goblet Cell?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Tracheal respiratory epithelium contains goblet cells. Terminal bronchioles and alveolar ducts normally lack them.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 5; source page 12.

questions.prompt: Which of the following options is wrong?
options: The lung bud appears in the 4th week of the fetal life.
In the last two weeks of fetal life, the amount of surfactant increases
Tracheal cartilages originate from the splanchnic mesoderm
The inner layer of the larynx is of mesodermal origin
questions.subject: embryology
questions.note: Laryngeal epithelial lining is endodermal; supporting cartilage/connective tissue is mesenchymal. The source uses fetal life loosely for the early embryonic fourth week.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 1; source page 13.

questions.prompt: Respiratory bronchioles appear in which of the following stages?
questions.subject: embryology
questions.note: Respiratory bronchioles emerge during the canalicular period; terminal bronchioles belong to the earlier conducting-tree stage.

evidence: Undated Tabiya respiratory photo paper; printed question 2; source page 13.

excludedItems.reason: Partial background view of physiology Q17 and neighboring sheets is duplicate incidental content; Q17 is fully retained from image 7.

audit.notes: All preferred source images visually reviewed; OCR used only as a drafting aid. All supplied complete items retained. Source annotations are unofficial, preserved separately from the audited answer. Null audited keys deliberately quarantine ambiguous or defective questions. Numbered options 1-4 and Persian letters are normalized to A-D in displayed order.

archive.title: Tabiya — 13-image annotated theory set
archive.note: Two albums (10 + 3 photos), same forwarder and original 23 July 2024 post. Now ordered by subject and printed question number: physiology 1-22, anatomy 1-11, histology 1-5, embryology 1-2. Q18 physiology is crossed out in the source; preserved, not silently removed. The date is a forwarding date, not a proven sitting date.
